title: Clear GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 with the smallest package-manager-generated lockfile update in apps/web
objective: The Dependency audit job fails on GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 (nanoid <3.3.18) in apps/web, on main and on every open pull request. Clear it honestly by moving the single pinned nanoid entry to the first patch release that satisfies the advisory floor, using the package manager rather than a hand-authored lockfile, and WITHOUT introducing the repository's first internal-host resolved URL. A security check made green by suppression rather than by fixing the underlying issue is the vacuous-green pattern this repository already exists to correct, so if the honest fix does not work the correct outcome is a report of failure, not a manufactured pass.
measured_premise: P1 MEASURED (apps/web at base 80c1684): npm audit --audit-level=high reproduces the advisory - nanoid <3.3.18, Severity high, GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8, '1 high severity vulnerability', 'fix available via npm audit fix' - at BARE exit code 1. Plain npm audit is identical, also bare exit 1. The failure is reproduced before any change, so the fix can be shown to fix something.

P2 MEASURED (lockfile at base): nanoid is pinned at 3.3.17, one patch release below the advisory floor. The earlier commit 26cc0dd moved 3.3.16 -> 3.3.17, which was then the highest 3.x available; 3.3.18 now resolves, so exactly one patch step remains. This is a genuine one-step bump, not a re-litigation of a closed fix.

P3 MEASURED: exactly ONE package depends on nanoid - postcss - and 3.3.18 satisfies its declared range. No postcss change is required, and nanoid stays on the CommonJS 3.x line, so postcss's require('nanoid/non-secure') keeps working. No major-version jump to the ESM-only 4/5 line is needed or permitted.

P3b DISCREPANCY RESOLVED, and the resolution corrects a proposed diagnosis rather than confirming it [M]: two sessions on this machine read different postcss facts - 8.5.25 requiring ^3.3.16 (mine) and 8.5.26 requiring ^3.3.17 (the orchestrator's) - and it was proposed that this was the package mirror serving inconsistent metadata within the hour. It is NOT. Both readings are correct, reproducible together in a single command, and they describe DIFFERENT THINGS: apps/web PINS and installs postcss 8.5.25, whose declared range is ^3.3.16, while the registry's dist-tags.latest is 8.5.26, whose declared range is ^3.3.17. Measured side by side from the same source in the same minute: postcss@8.5.25 -> ^3.3.16, postcss@8.5.26 -> ^3.3.17, dist-tags.latest -> 8.5.26, and the copy actually installed on disk after npm ci -> 8.5.25 requiring ^3.3.16. The mirror was self-consistent on this point; the difference is installed-and-pinned versus registry-latest. The authoritative reading for THIS repository is the pinned one, because that is the version the lockfile installs. Both ranges are satisfied by 3.3.18 either way, so every conclusion drawn from either reading survives - but the instrument was not at fault, and recording it as flaky would have entrenched a false explanation.
P4 MEASURED (lockfile at base): 336 resolved URLs, 336 of them on registry.npmjs.org, ZERO on any other host. 336 integrity entries: 335 sha1- and 1 sha512-.

P5 MEASURED: this machine's configured npm registry is an internal proxy, and public registry.npmjs.org is NOT reachable from here (HTTPS request fails at transport level; an independent fetch path fails the same way). Any package-manager write therefore risks rewriting resolved to an internal host, which would become the repository's FIRST non-public resolved host. This is a hard disclosure boundary, not a style preference.

P6 MEASURED (positive control on the derivation METHOD): upstream dist.shasum for nanoid 3.3.17 is f1c3aa253c52547956a52c50bff754316f61037a; converting that hex digest to base64 yields sha1-8cOqJTxSVHlWpSxQv/dUMW9hA3o=, which is EXACTLY the value already committed at base and already known to work. The method is validated against a known-good oracle inside the repository rather than trusted.

P7 MEASURED: upstream dist.shasum for nanoid 3.3.18 is f66a2de1199ffde0fcf21c8a5f13106b1c081913, giving sha1-9mot4Rmf/eD88hyKXxMQaxwIGRM=. The fetched 5713-byte tarball recomputes to that same sha1 digest, so the served bytes are NOT re-packed and the integrity value corresponds to the genuine published artifact. Its sha512 is DTg4MJbGMWkfi6VZFdNt2/caMbQy4Ou+Op/hJQvGEWcnVfoA1QA+xzRKAzw9jD6+GVOOeYr/mIcuDSdug6F6+w== , recorded for cross-reference.

P8 MEASURED: a sha512 dist.integrity field is ABSENT from the metadata reachable here, which explains the 335/336 sha1 convention - it is what the metadata source supplies, not a stylistic choice. Matching the convention is therefore also the option that avoids inventing a digest the toolchain did not produce.

P9 MEASURED (.github/workflows/ci.yml): the node job runs npm ci at the REPOSITORY ROOT only. No CI job runs npm ci, npm test, or a production build inside apps/web. A wrong integrity value in apps/web/package-lock.json would therefore NOT be caught by any current CI gate, so it must be proved locally rather than deferred to CI.

P10 MEASURED: scripts/check_urls.py is a repository-owned allowlist guard that scans every tracked text file including lockfiles and fails on any non-allowlisted host. It is used here as an INDEPENDENT oracle for the disclosure requirement, so the non-internal-host claim does not rest on my own grep alone.
in_scope: apps/web/package-lock.json - the single node_modules/nanoid entry only (version, resolved, integrity)
out_of_scope_zero_diff: apps/web/package.json - no new override, no dependency change. The pre-existing vite/esbuild/js-yaml overrides are NOT touched and no nanoid override is added.
.github/** - no audit-level relaxation, no suppression, no allowlisting, no new or altered job
any .npmrc, audit configuration, or registry configuration in the repository
agent-state/feature_list.json - byte-identical to base; no ledger flag is flipped
apps/api/**, apps/worker/**, tests/**, scripts/**, migrations/**, docs/**
merge or promotion of the pull request
acceptance_criteria: A1: npm audit in apps/web reports 'found 0 vulnerabilities' at BARE exit code 0, for both plain npm audit and npm audit --audit-level=high. Exit codes read from a bare invocation, never through a pipeline that can corrupt LASTEXITCODE.
A2: git diff --numstat shows the change confined to apps/web/package-lock.json plus agent-state files, and the lockfile diff is exactly 3 insertions and 3 deletions in a single hunk.
A3: the nanoid entry reads version 3.3.18, resolved https://registry.npmjs.org/nanoid/-/nanoid-3.3.18.tgz, integrity sha1-9mot4Rmf/eD88hyKXxMQaxwIGRM=.
A4: the FINAL lockfile contains 336 resolved URLs, all on registry.npmjs.org, and ZERO on any other host - proved by direct count AND independently by scripts/check_urls.py.
A5: npm ci in apps/web succeeds from the COMMITTED lockfile at bare exit 0 and leaves the lockfile blob hash unchanged.
A6: apps/web tests pass and the production build (tsc -b && vite build) succeeds.
A7: scripts/check.ps1 -NodeAudit reports ALL CHECKS PASSED at exit 0.
A8: the full Python suite result is unchanged relative to base.
A9: no override, no audit suppression, no --audit-level relaxation, no GitHub tarball source, no public-registry bypass, no nanoid 4/5 jump.
A10: no internal hostname appears in any committed file, commit message, pull request body, or progress note.
verification_plan: V1: bare npm audit and npm audit --audit-level=high in apps/web, before and after, with exit codes captured from a bare call.
V2: git diff --numstat over the whole tree, and git diff on the lockfile hunk.
V3: host census of the final lockfile by regex over every resolved URL, grouped by host, plus the total http(s) host census.
V5: rm -rf node_modules then npm ci in apps/web; re-hash the lockfile blob afterwards to prove npm did not rewrite it.
V6: npm test and npm run build in apps/web.
V8: full pytest run, compared against the base result.
negative_tests: N1: the advisory must be REPRODUCED before the change, otherwise a green afterwards proves nothing. Done: bare exit 1 at base.
N2: prove the green is not a suppression - diff must show no package.json override change, no .npmrc, no audit configuration, no CI flag change.
N3: npm ci verifies integrity against the lockfile, so a wrong hash fails loudly; a passing npm ci is therefore positive evidence the digest matches the bytes the package manager actually fetches.
N4: prove the resolved host did not silently become internal using the repository's own allowlist guard, not only my own grep.
N5: confirm the sha1 derivation method reproduces the already-committed 3.3.17 value before applying it to 3.3.18.
disclosed_limitations: L1: public registry.npmjs.org cannot be contacted from this machine, so the integrity value could not be checked against a byte stream fetched directly from the public host. The claim rests instead on the upstream-published dist.shasum, on a byte-level recomputation of the fetched tarball agreeing with it, and on a positive control proving the same derivation reproduces the already-committed and already-working 3.3.17 value.

L2: because no CI job installs apps/web (P9), CI cannot confirm the integrity value against the public registry either. This is disclosed rather than presented as covered, and is a candidate follow-up: apps/web has a lockfile, 9 test files, a tsc -b type-check and a Dockerfile that runs npm ci, and CI performs exactly ONE operation against it - an audit that reads the lockfile without installing. Web tests, TypeScript type-checking and the production build therefore never run in CI at all. Out of scope for a lockfile bump; filed as an observation, not fixed here.

L3: the sha1 integrity convention is inherited, not chosen. It is weaker than sha512, and this change neither improves nor worsens it - it follows the file's existing 335/336 convention and the digest the metadata source supplies. Strengthening the whole lockfile to sha512 would be a separate, deliberate slice, not a side effect of an advisory fix.
data_implications: None. No schema, migration, fixture, catalogue record, or evidence artefact is touched.
security_privacy: This IS the security fix - it removes a high-severity advisory from the build-time dependency surface that apps/web/Dockerfile installs to produce the shipped static assets. It also carries a disclosure risk in the opposite direction: a package-manager write on this machine can rewrite resolved to an internal feed host. That risk is gated by A4, A10, N4 and by scripts/check_urls.py.
portability: Unchanged. nanoid remains on the CommonJS 3.x line, so postcss keeps working; no runtime, service, framework or provider dependency is added.
z0_risk: None. No classification, quota, offer, provider or publication logic is touched.
